AI-soldiers are simple riflemen who becomes less effective at higher difficulty.

The best character is the Demolisher, then comes the Technican, then the Gunner, after this the Doc and the most nerfed character is the Phalanx. 

The Gunner is a GREAT contribution to any team with it´s OVERCLOCK ability. 

The turret of the Technician gives bonuses to everybody close to it and can be upgraded. 

The Trauma Station of the Doc gives healing to nearby soldiers and can be upgraded. But the Combat Stims of the Doc is not as impressive, with increased accuracy, stability, stamina reg and increased movement speed. All of this sounds great but have little impact on the game. 

The shield of the Phalanx looks impressive, but it ONLY blocks "normal attacks". 
"Special attacks" ignores the shield and makes it worthless. 
The secondary ability of the Phalanx is ONLY useful if a lot of enemies are swarming up close - but this means certain death on higher difficulty, because the ability takes it´s sweet time to activate.

The guns (rifles, shotguns, pistols) is a balance of damage and rate-of-fire. 
The higher the damage, the lower the rate-of-fire. You need a balance of these things. But personally I like to have one gun with high damage and another gun with high rate-of-fire. 

But NEVER use the M95 Grenade launcher. Sure, it has a high damage, BUT it only goes off when it FEELS like it. 
Also the "Minigun" is a TOTAL joke. It is like a copy from a 19th century gatling gun. 
The rate-of-fire is very low compared to a "real" minigun and it sounds like some kind of old auto-cannon. 

Also AVOID the Laserpistol. Sure, it has unlimited ammo, BUT It "charges up" before every shot wich means that every shot WILL miss, unless you are fireing at a stationary target. It ALSO OVERHEATS VERY FAST and that makes it TOTALLY USELESS for a few seconds. 

The sidearm is ALWAYS the same and can NEVER be upgraded. This is very disappointing.

Overall, the Game in its current state is a 6/10 – it just about scrapes it’s (at time of writing) price of £30; but once I think they develop the core options and address the other flaws then I think FireTeam could be one of the "Better" Aliens franchise games out there - it won't be the best purely because this style game isn't everyone's preference; but it is a solid entry. I’d say it sits somewhere between Gears of Wars, The Division and Left 4 Dead in terms of gameplay. It’s a fun if somewhat familiar formula but not everyone’s game of choice.

Now then: The loop is pretty solid - go to mission, kill aliens, get XP, level up your guns, get new perks to become more powerful; rerun the content on higher difficulty. Rinse and repeat. You get to unlock decals, colours and various Hats to give your marine some character/ customization. There's a collectables system which unlocks lore/dialogue, and the gunplay is pretty solid. A real strong point is the perks/skills system. A lot of perks are useable across classes so you are encouraged to play and level everything and then build and tweak your setup to your playstyle. 

It also has a daily/weekly quest system as well you can log into this every day and grab a nice reward for a quick 30-1hrs play. The grind/padding aspects of the game are quite reasonable in my opinion and maximum respect to ColdIron for not going the paid-loot box direction that this game could have gone down. A further nice little touch is that some of the dialogue and mission objectives change on run to run; so there a good chance to get a little mix to the mission experience each time. Also, intense and insane difficulties are hilarious with friends simply because you can accidently one shot a mis-positioned teammate and keeping your cool and spacing does become quite a fun challenge. Though I hope in future we will be able to swap out the AI bots in private games for particular builds or even just Bots marine skins – as running with synths only emphasises some of the problems of the game, and you have no personalities to engage with unlike games like L4D where even despite their bad AI at least the Bots had some character quirks to them.

As this title develops, I really think content is going to be key here to keep a steady player base; as well as entice back those who play between patches. Not just hats and new guns either. I’m talking a lot more campaigns, extra horde mode levels and modifiers, more marine editing options - like fatigue colours; as well as some QOL features like a "Try before you buy" targeting range, and completed mission by difficulty tracking. 

A big problem however is that regardless of how much content they add; the thing that needs major addressing is the matchmaking system. It's absolutely terrible because of how the math works out. I'm lucky in that I have a squad of friends I can run with; but playing solo outside casual or standard difficulties is tedious at best as you end up with bots frequently – so may as well-run private games. I can really see the game going one of two ways: either upping the quality of the AI squad-mates and making the campaign into something that’s quite lengthy (12+ campaigns with 36+ possible missions) for people to run on casual-intense and shift it more towards a single player/friends group experience. Or they turn matchmaker into a random mission drop button. I’m hoping for the former because I can’t see the game sustaining a large community beyond a few years. It also won’t surprise me if this ends up on Xbox Game Pass and PS Now over Christmas to try inject more people into the community. 

Overall Cold Iron have a good starting point here. I hope they develop it further and just have fun with it. They could throw out new storylines, characters etc without any real risk of messing it up. Prometheus and Covenant set the Aliens universe lore bar quite low, whilst Colonial Marine set that even lower for video games.

Edit: And Just like that they add random Que Quick Play. Now it's 7/10

This game is a lot of fun, and just what I was looking for as a long-term Aliens fan. It really looks the part too - the first few levels are fairly standard industrial-complex-with-corridors, but the later levels have some gorgeous details and viewpoints. The weapon perks and abilities are somewhat confusing to make sense of at the beginning, but there's some good depth there with the combinations of bonuses you can make. 

It doesn't necessarily feel like it has a lot of legs - I can't see myself playing it for longer than a few months, unless the DLC has some surprises in store - but I'm a huge Aliens fan and this one really hit the spot. Having a maximum of three people on a team is a good number, and makes for some tense firefights. It's structured around a multiplayer campaign, where you and two squadmates play through a series of missions. There appears to be a story, but it's fairly barebones and seems to be just a mechanism to let the voice on the comms to tell you where to go and what button to press. The only thing obviously missing is that the pulse rifle doesn't have an attached grenade launcher (sorely needed for a one-click grenade) - I really hope that's coming in a DLC!

The alien AI isn't very smart, but it doesn't need to be. It just needs to swarm you and try and overwhelm you, and it does that consistently well (with a good few surprises which is nice). They do appear to follow pre-authored navigation paths in some cases though, which makes them a little too easy to pick off, and their animation is quite stiff at times and not fluid, which makes them less scary than they otherwise would be.

The audio is spot on, from gun sounds to the "jump scare" signature stinger when you get a headshot. However it was a big let down for me to not hear the original James Horner score anywhere - I like Austin Wintory's work in general, but I think he missed the mark on this one.

We had heard that the standard difficulty is on the easy side, so we initially went for the next highest setting and got our asses handed to us (in a fun way!). So we went back to the standard difficulty in order to build up our gear & perks, but it really is too easy - there's not  much fear of dying. It was still fun though, and you do feel like a badass when the team is working together and beating back the swarm. The gunplay is good in general, and the shotgun is particularly satisfying (I keep it handy for close encounters). There are a lot of weapon mods and perks which you can use in-game currency to buy, and no doubt helps you to tackle the higher difficulties. I'm not sure that's enough for long-term replayability though; since the campaign is linear, once you've seen an area then you very quickly know what to expect, which takes some of the fun out of things. Some of the best bits of the game are when you're nervous and not knowing what direction the aliens are going to come from.

[Edit - I had a problem with playing on a 32:9 ultrawide, but that got sorted in the latest patch - many thanks!]

Overall it's a big thumbs up from me.

Generally the attempt at an Alien coop-shooter is admirable but the execution could be done better.
There are a couple of things I hope to see the developers could consider working on. I will briefly summarize it up here based on my own opinion.

1) The AI for both ally android and aliens need much improvement. The aliens' path-finding algorithm is extremely predictable and straight-forward, making them easy targets to pick off once you realize it. Unlike the franchise where aliens display high level of intelligence to ambush the characters, over here feels like the opposite. The fear of being overrun from all sides is absent and further decreases the thrilling aspect expected of an Alien game.

Your friendly androids here though fare slightly better than the Aliens, it leaves much room for improvement. From time to time it can get stuck at certain junctions and does not distance itself from the approaching aliens. They always spawn as gunner class which can be quite boring after a couple of runs with them.

2) I love how the story telling have been done so far but the severe lack of new game contents or game patches made me wonder if the developers themselves have already given up on Aliens Fireteam before me. I do find it commendable to see the addition of new Phalanx class but its shielding capabilities and overall effectiveness in a team play leaves me questioning its purpose than awe.

Playable campaigns are way too short for any excitement and its progression are linear in design. It could do better should there be at least an alternative route in each mission to allow branching of different pathway to the next mission. This would intrigue players' exploration instincts and provide an opportunity to further expand on game contents. The horde mode desperately needs more maps and rewards for Xth number of rounds cleared. Otherwise it feels mindlessly repetitive and diminishes enjoyment. The random spawn of alien variants with mixed abilities would spice up the challenge for players. New weapon and weapon attachments additions that provide certain degree of synergy with other weapons could prove to be an appeal towards effective team play.

3) Overall game design and UI could use some additional improvements. The matchmaking mechanism is...terrible to say and I shall leave it at that. There should be checkpoints available for continuation after a team wipe instead of restarting from the very beginning. Some may say it poses a challenge but I say the lack of it makes the gameplay experience extremely painful during a team wipe. Game sessions in progress should have an option to allow players to join anytime. This could also include an option for players to go with a 4-men team instead of 3 which currently feels awkward in my opinion. I would love to have an option to enable 1st-person-view because that would be more exciting. In the case of a multiplayer game session, it would be good to display the player's portrait as part of the UI for a more personalized experience, given that STEAM does have these features available. The lack of voice chat feature in a shooter game is quite unthinkable; if not providing an option to send standard radio voice commands for players to coordinate their action should be considered.

In conclusion, I feel that Aliens Fireteam has so much potential to become a better game and I hate to say that current state of the game is giving me an impression of an unpolished rushed out game. My personal scoring for this game would at best be 5.5/10 for the price point and its mediocre game play experience.

Cant really recommend this game confidently to anyone, at least for now.

Do NOT buy this game until matchmaking is fixed.  You'll only drive yourself crazy trying to find a game.

Whatever potential this game has is negated by the non-existent match making system.  At time of writing, there is no game lobby browser.  To find a game you either need to spam an unofficial Discord channel, or load up a game and change the map and/or difficulty at random in hopes you find somebody who also happens to be looking to do that exact same map and difficulty at that exact moment.  Even then I've encountered people who get disconnected and do not load into a map.  Because this game also does not have drop-in sessions, that means you're either playing solo or duo.

***Update: 16 Oct, 2021 @ 14:45 GMT+8***
Game is dead.  Under 1,000 players worldwide.  Save yourself time, money and frustration and go play Back 4 Blood instead.
